texts.preamble: Yellamma vs The State Of Telangana on 27 March, 2023 Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili And The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik Writ Petition No.2388 Of 2023 Order:
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that the detenu was detained by the respondents vide impugned detention order, dated 21.01.2023, by invoking the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 on the alleged ground that he was involved in six crimes i.e. Crime Nos.221 of 2022 and 222 of 2022 of Rayaparthy Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 420, 468 and 471 I.P.C; Crime No.629 of 2022 of A.J. Mills Colony Police Station, registered for the offences under Sections 420 and 468 I.P.C.; Crime No.630 of 2022 of A.J. Mills Colony Police Station, Warangal Commissionerate, registered for the offence under Section 420 I.P.C.; Crime No.294 of 2022 of Dornakal Police Station, Mahabubabad District, registered for the offences under Sections 406, 468 and 471 read with 34 I.P.C.; and Crime No.357 of 2022 of Khammam I Town Police Station, Khammam District, registered for the offence under Section 420 I.P.C. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the detenu was arrested on 23.12.2022 in connection with Crime Nos.629 of 2022 and 630 of 3 AKS,J & PK,J 2022 of A.J. Mills Colony Police Station and his Yellamma vs The State Of Telangana on 27 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114443039/ 1 arrest was regularized in the remaining crimes through PT warrants. The detenu was granted bail in Crime Nos.221 of 2022, 222 of 2022, 629 of 2022 and 630 of 2022 and in the remaining two crimes i.e. Crime Nos.294 of 2022 and 357 of 2022, the bail applications moved by the detenu are still pending. Thus, the detenu continues to be in judicial custody as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order. The detaining authority, without application of mind, has passed the impugned detention order on the ground that the detenu is causing inconvenience and disturbance to the general public. Learned counsel further contended that when the detenu is in jail on judicial remand, the question of the detenu disturbing the peace and tranquility in the society would not arise. The impugned orders are passed without application of mind. Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the Writ Petition by setting aside the impugned orders, as admittedly, as on the date of passing of the impugned detention order, the detenu is in judicial remand. 5. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that the detenu was involved in six crimes of serious nature and there is every possibility of the detenu being enlarged on bail.
